investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T12:09–12:16Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no node can accept a new peer-pod VM. Because the pod never starts, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-20 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating that the 6-node cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract to fail entirely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 124–145 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; the impact is localized to the AURA observability eval suite for the remote-agents feature in production-api.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — no capacity available for new peer-pod VMs, causing all remote-agent pod submissions to be immediately Unschedulable with no preemption path.

[Likely contributing] Only 2 of 6 cluster nodes satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector for remote agent workloads; the remaining 4 nodes are structurally ineligible, meaning the effective scheduling pool is small and easily saturated.

[Possible] A prior eval run, a leaked agent pod from a previous withCleanup failure, or another workload is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes without releasing them, preventing new allocations.

[Possible] The cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or node capacity was reduced (e.g., node maintenance, node removal, or resource limit change) without a corresponding reduction in concurrent remote-agent workload, shrinking available capacity below the demand floor.

[Lower likelihood] A node affinity/selector misconfiguration on the submitted pod could have narrowed the eligible node set further, but the message explicitly names 2 nodes as capacity-insufficient rather than affinity-mismatched, making this a secondary concern.

If re-running the eval immediately after this failure produces a passing result with all 5 evidence fields present, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval's pods were released) rather than a sustained capacity deficit.

If the 2 nodes flagged as 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' are found to have been removed from the cluster or placed into maintenance between the eval run and investigation, the cause would be node unavailability rather than resource exhaustion on healthy nodes.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to further restrict eligible nodes (reducing the pool below 2), the root cause would shift to a configuration change rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime is found in the history (lastPassingAt is currently null due to previousRunCount=0), it would establish a baseline and help determine whether this is a regression or a first-run failure.
